comments.body:
I've checked the `~/Library/Preferences`folder and can't find a `plist` belongs to ice.

The file in `~Library/Preferences` should be called `com.jordanbaird.Ice.plist`.

If you still can't find it, you can run the following command in Terminal:

```
defaults export com.jordanbaird.Ice ~/Desktop/Ice.plist
```

And then import it on your new machine with:

```
defaults import com.jordanbaird.Ice ~/Desktop/Ice.plist
```

> [!Note]

Yes I want that really bad

For anyone here who just wants the settings in a readable file for their dotfiles, I wrote a small read only command that does that part: https://pypi.org/project/iceprefs/ (`pip install iceprefs`, source at https://github.com/Rezarys/iceprefs, MIT).

`defaults export com.jordanbaird.Ice` plus `plutil -convert json` already gets you most of the way. The gap it fills is the rest: Ice stores hotkeys and the Ice icon as data blobs holding JSON, so those come out of `plutil` as base64 and a diff between two machines says nothing about them. `iceprefs` unwraps them, and prints hotkeys as key names rather than virtual key codes, so `ToggleHiddenSection` reads as `⌃⌘I` instead of a base64 string.

It only reads. There is no import side, since `defaults import` already does that.

Honest reserve, and I would rather say it here than have someone find out: I have not run it against a real Ice profile, only against fixtures written for its tests. The file layout, the hotkey encoding and the modifier mask come from reading the Ice source. If you try it on your own profile and something comes out wrong, an issue with what you saw would help a lot.

Not affiliated with Ice or with its author. "Ice" is in the name only to say which file the tool reads, and I will rename it right away if that is not welcome.

Built with AI assistance, reviewed and tested by me.

if (appsWithUpdatesCount)
